request.spec:
A rate may carry a to-date as well as a from-date (RATE_SET gains to=<date> at the end when one
was given; a to-date before the from-date is refused). A rate applies through its to-date; a claim
dated after the to-date of the rate that would apply to it, with no later rate in force on the
claim's date, has due n/a, and everything that reads due follows (a total skips it, a statement
binds n/a, the late charge has nothing to add to).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A rate may carry a to-date as well as a from-date (RATE_SET gains to=<date> at the end when one
was given; a to-date before the from-date is refused). A rate applies through its to-date; a claim
dated after the to-date of the rate that would apply to it, with no later rate in force on the
claim's date, has due n/a, and everything that reads due follows (a total skips it, a statement
binds n/a, the late charge has nothing to add to).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Rates can now have a to-date as well as a from-date, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**How a rate is chosen now:** a claim still takes the rate with the latest from-date on or before its date. If the claim is dated after that rate's to-date, its due is n/a. It does not fall back to an earlier rate. This is now in one place on the server (`Rate.inForce`), used by the rate lookup, the rollup and the statement code. The screen's own check (`pctOn` in `rates.ts`) follows the same rule, so totals, statements and the "in force today" figures all agree. The late charge was already skipped when there's no due, so it needed no change.

**What changed:**
- **Stored data:** new migration `V33__rate_to.sql` adds a `to_date` column to rates.
- **Server:** the rate save accepts and returns `to`. A to-date before the from-date is refused with a 400 and nothing is saved or audited. `RATE_SET` adds ` to=<date>` at the end when one was given. Setting a grade and from-date again replaces its to-date too, so leaving it blank removes the end date.
- **Screen:** a "To" field (`rate-form-to`) that the form checks before sending, and a `rate-to` column in the rates table.

**One rule I added that the request didn't spell out.** Normally a person's due-total is n/a when their grade has no rate in force today. The first test expects otherwise: with today's rate ended, Ada's total is still 1.00, from a claim priced under the earlier start rate. So a due earned under any rate other than today's now counts toward the total, the same way a settled or stated due already did. Without this, the total would stay n/a. The rule is applied the same way on screen, in the rollup and in statements.

That rule has a side effect beyond end dates: if a grade's only rate starts in the future and a claim is dated after that start, the person's total now shows that claim's due instead of n/a.
